newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. debt futures up, but downtrend intact.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. debt futures up, but downtrend intact.

text.p: U.S. debt futures were slightly higher, but the intermediate-term downtrend is intact going into Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, technical analysts said.
"It's still a sell-strength type of rally," said Michael Krauss, chief technical strategist at Chase Securities Inc.

Krauss and other analysts said short-term technical factors were supporting modest gains in both June bonds and September Eurodollars. They noted that June T-bonds in particular were holding above support at about 108-16/32.
The 108-16/32 to 108-25/32 area is equivalent to a bond yield of seven percent, they said. Meanwhile, the yield on the 10-year note was holding support at 6.77 percent, Krauss said.
A rise to 109-18, or a bond yield of 6.91 percent, would confirm that a short-term low had been established and that the market would gravitate higher, Krauss said.
Steve Boyajian, director of technical analysis at MMS International, said the market could stage a rally to 110-00 and possibly 110-14/32, the March 7 high, if June rises through the pivot point.
Boyajian pegged the pivot point at 109-08/32.
Stewart Taylor, an analyst with the Taylor Fixed-Income Outlook, put the pivot point at 108-30/32, and noted that last week was the second weekly close below the pivot.
Taylor said the bond futures market on a weekly continuation chart closed below the uptrend from the 1994 low basis the March contract, which expired on Friday.
"I believe that the only chance that the market has to save itself is to rally and post an immediate close back above the trendline," Taylor wrote in his daily outlook.
However, analysts said the defensive tone in notes and Eurodollars dampened any bullish prospects for bonds.
"The rebound is encouraging but it's mostly localized in the bonds, so it's still a concern," Boyajian said.
He noted that September Eurodollars' close at 93.81 on Friday was below a significant support level at 93.89, and that June, September and December broke to new lows for the year on Friday.

Support is now seen at Thursday and Friday's daily low of 93.79, and at 93.76, the 50-percent retracement level of last year's rise, Krauss said. He said 93.69, the uptrend line from the low of November 1994, should hold as support in the intermediate term.
The two-year note to 30-year bond spread still reflects a flattening yield curve bias and is approaching levels that triggered profit-taking in the last year and a half, Boyajian said.
Currently the two- to 30-year spread stood at 67 basis points, near the December 1995 low of 62.3 bps, he said. (Chicago DerivativesDesk 312-408-8750))
